courseDescription: TEMPORARY UNREVIEWED AI-GENERATED SAMPLE. English to Piedmontais (Piedmontese), with 24 Lessons demonstrating the 24 current named Exercise types. The content is for testing and requires native-speaker review before language-teaching use. Basic spellings were checked against Claudio Panero's English-Piedmontese dictionary; examples and letter diagrams are newly authored. Audio uses On-Device TTS with pms-IT. This demo contains no recorded Piedmontais voice. Listening examples require a suitable device voice; availability and pronunciation depend on the device.

lessons.title: Choose — First words

content.text: pan = bread; gat = cat; eva = water. Choose the Piedmontais word.
Choose: First words. Three short examples use this exercise type.

prompt.text: How do you say bread in Piedmontais?
How do you say cat in Piedmontais?
How do you say water in Piedmontais?

lessons.title: Fill in the blank — Small phrases

content.text: ël can = the dog; la ca = the house; bon-a matin = good morning.
Fill in the blank: Small phrases. Three short examples use this exercise type.

prompt.text: Complete the phrase meaning the dog.
Complete the phrase meaning the house.
Complete the greeting meaning good morning.

lessons.title: Select the image — Words in pictures

content.text: Look at the pictures: gat = cat; pan = bread; eva = water.
Select the image: Words in pictures. Three short examples use this exercise type.

lessons.title: Recognize characters — Accented letters

content.text: These letter diagrams distinguish ë (e with diaeresis), é (e with acute accent), and ò (o with grave accent). Identify the printed character, not its sound.
Recognize characters: Accented letters. Three short examples use this exercise type.

prompt.text: Which accented e is printed here?

lessons.title: What do you hear — Hear a greeting

content.text: bondì = good morning; mersì = thank you; ciàu = hello or bye. Choose the exact written word you hear. Audio uses On-Device TTS with pms-IT. This demo contains no recorded Piedmontais voice. Listening examples require a suitable device voice; availability and pronunciation depend on the device.
What do you hear: Hear a greeting. Three short examples use this exercise type.

lessons.title: Listen and choose — Listen for meaning

content.text: I l'hai = I have; i son = I am; a ca = at home; lìber = book; un = one; doi = two; tre = three. Listen to each short passage and answer its English question. Audio uses On-Device TTS with pms-IT. This demo contains no recorded Piedmontais voice. Listening examples require a suitable device voice; availability and pronunciation depend on the device.
Listen and choose: Listen for meaning. Three short examples use this exercise type.

prompt.text: Mi i son a ca. I l'hai un lìber.
I l'hai un gat e un can.
La lista: pan, eva e tre pom.
How many apples are on the list?

lessons.title: Reading comprehension — Read a short note

content.text: la lista = the list; pan = bread; eva = water; pom = apple; gat = cat; can = dog; lìber = book; a ca = at home.
Reading comprehension: Read a short note. Three short examples use this exercise type.

prompt.text: La lista: pan, eva e tre pom.
Which drink is on the list?
I l'hai un gat e un can.
How many kinds of animal does the speaker have?
Mi i son a ca. I l'hai un lìber.

lessons.title: Dialogue response — Reply politely

content.text: bondì = good morning; grassie = thank you; prego = you are welcome; bon-aneuit = good night. The situation determines the reply.
Dialogue response: Reply politely. Three short examples use this exercise type.

prompt.text: It is morning. Return Anna's greeting.
Anna thanks you. Choose you are welcome.
You are going to bed. Return the good-night wish.

lessons.title: Contextual comprehension — Who said it

content.text: Read the two speakers' words. I l'hai means I have. Keep track of who owns the object or responds to the other speaker.
Contextual comprehension: Who said it. Three short examples use this exercise type.

lessons.title: Type the translation — Write in Piedmontais

content.text: Translate English into Piedmontais. Thank you accepts grassie or mersì. The happy speaker is masculine: i son content; mi is optional. The house is la ca.
Type the translation: Write in Piedmontais. Three short examples use this exercise type.

lessons.title: Build the translation — Translate with blocks

content.text: Build an English phrase in Piedmontais. ël lìber = the book; i son content = I am happy (masculine); pan e eva = bread and water. For I am happy, both mi i son content and i son content are accepted.
Build the translation: Translate with blocks. Three short examples use this exercise type.

lessons.title: Pick the translation (to target) — English to Piedmontais

content.text: Read the English source and pick its Piedmontais translation. ël can = the dog; ross = red; tre = three.
Pick the translation (to target): English to Piedmontais. Three short examples use this exercise type.

lessons.title: Pick the translation (to source) — Piedmontais to English

content.text: Read the Piedmontais source and pick its English meaning. bon-aneuit = good night; ël pan = the bread; mi i son content = I am happy.
Pick the translation (to source): Piedmontais to English. Three short examples use this exercise type.

lessons.title: Type a missing word — Complete a phrase

content.text: Type only the missing word. ël lìber = the book; la ca = the house; pan e eva = bread and water. Preserve the accent in lìber.
Type a missing word: Complete a phrase. Three short examples use this exercise type.

lessons.title: Type the missing word — First-letter help

content.text: Complete each missing word after its first letter is shown. Enter the whole word: gat (cat), ca (house), or lìber (book), including the first letter.
Type the missing word: First-letter help. Three short examples use this exercise type.

exercise.hint: An object with pages to read.

lessons.title: Type what you hear — Hear and spell

content.text: Listen and type the whole word. The vocabulary is pan (bread), eva (water), and pom (apple). Audio uses On-Device TTS with pms-IT. This demo contains no recorded Piedmontais voice. Listening examples require a suitable device voice; availability and pronunciation depend on the device.
Type what you hear: Hear and spell. Three short examples use this exercise type.

lessons.title: Listen for missing words — Listen for gaps

content.text: The transcript supplies the sentence around each missing word. Fill the missing words in order: pan = bread; eva = water; gat = cat; can = dog; lìber = book. Audio uses On-Device TTS with pms-IT. This demo contains no recorded Piedmontais voice. Listening examples require a suitable device voice; availability and pronunciation depend on the device.
Listen for missing words: Listen for gaps. Three short examples use this exercise type.

I l'hai un gat e un can.

lessons.title: Match the pairs — Everyday pairs

content.text: Match each English meaning with its Piedmontais phrase. Pair relationships stay the same when the display is shuffled.
Match the pairs: Everyday pairs. Three short examples use this exercise type.

Match each Piedmontais phrase with its English meaning.

lessons.title: Match the words — Three translations

content.text: Match English words with Piedmontais words. Food: pan, eva, pom. Animals: gat, can, caval. At home: tàula, cadrega, pòrta.
Match the words: Three translations. Three short examples use this exercise type.

prompt.text: Match English food and drink words to Piedmontais.
Match English animal words to Piedmontais.

lessons.title: Match related words — Related Piedmontais words

content.text: Follow the relationship named in each exercise. Opposites: càud/frèid (hot/cold), nèir/bianch (black/white), grand/cit (big/small). Plurals: ël lìber/ij lìber, la ca/le ca, la cadrega/le cadreghe. Articles: ël gat, la ca, ël lìber.
Match related words: Related Piedmontais words. Three short examples use this exercise type.

prompt.text: Match each singular phrase to its plural.
Match each noun to the same noun with its definite article.

lessons.title: Listen and match — Match what you hear

content.text: Play each Piedmontais item and match it to the English meaning. Each exercise has three unique audio/text pairs and no distractors. Audio uses On-Device TTS with pms-IT. This demo contains no recorded Piedmontais voice. Listening examples require a suitable device voice; availability and pronunciation depend on the device.
Listen and match: Match what you hear. Three short examples use this exercise type.

prompt.text: Match each spoken Piedmontais food or drink word to its English meaning.

Match each spoken Piedmontais colour word to its English meaning.

lessons.title: Word order — Put words in order

content.text: Restore the Piedmontais phrase. Keep i before son. A repeated ël needs its own block each time. These are ordering exercises; no English sentence is being translated.
Word order: Put words in order. Three short examples use this exercise type.

prompt.text: Put the speaker, verb and description in order.
Put the food first, then the link, then the drink.
Put the cat first and the dog second, with an article before each.

lessons.title: Image-prompt ordering — Build pictured words

content.text: Use every letter to spell the Piedmontais word in the picture: pan (bread), gat (cat), caval (horse). The two a letters in caval are separate blocks.
Image-prompt ordering: Build pictured words. Three short examples use this exercise type.

prompt.text: Spell the pictured food in Piedmontais.
Spell the pictured pet in Piedmontais.
Spell the pictured farm animal in Piedmontais.
